extracted.intended_audience: poets, creative writers, and literary readers (19th-century Atlantic Monthly contributors/readers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and satirical commentary on composing pastoral and topical verse with an emphasis on local observation, vivid diction, and avoiding clichés or merely printed/borrowed images. Also contains notes on how oral eloquence differs from text for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid relying on printed portrayals or secondhand images
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't go blind on the word o' noospaper or poet! They're apt to puff, an' May-day seldom looks Up in the country ez it doos in books;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text warns writers (and readers) not to accept newspaper or poetic depictions as authoritative for lived experience — printed May-day often differs from the country reality. Prefer firsthand observation over secondhand or bookish images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer live, local particulars to printed generalities
rubrics_metrics.description: I'd give more for one live bobolink Than a square mile o' larks in printer's ink,
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete, local, living detail (a single real bobolink) is more valuable in poetry than massed, clichéd printed images. Use specific natural particulars to give authenticity and weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware early-reading influences and avoid derivative subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Jes' so with poets: wut they've airly read Gits kind o' worked into their heart an' head, So's't they can't seem to write but jest on sheers With furrin countries or played-out ideers,
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should recognize how formative reading shapes their instincts and avoid defaulting to foreign or exhausted themes. Strive for originality rooted in one's own experience rather than imitation of worn topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid catalogue (list-like) descriptive style
rubrics_metrics.description: I don't love your cat'logue style,-- Ez if to sell off Natur' by vendoo;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The poet criticizes a flattened, inventory-like mode of description. Instead of listing items, prioritize selective, impactful details that convey feeling and scene.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer a single vivid, embodied word over many generic ones
rubrics_metrics.description: One word with blood in 't's twice ez good ez two: 'nuff sed,
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Economy and concreteness: choose precise, visceral words that carry life and specificity rather than padding a line with multiple weak terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Render seasonal and natural phenomena with accurate, local sequence
rubrics_metrics.description: I, country-born an' bred, know where to find Some blooms thet make the season suit the mind, ... Thet's Northun natur', slow an' apt to doubt, But when it _doos_ git stirred, ther' 's no gin-out!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depict seasons and nature in the order and character they actually present locally (e.g., arrival of blackbirds, maples, robins, then full spring). Local seasonal truth lends credibility and emotional resonance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize differences between oral eloquence and written text
rubrics_metrics.description: What passes without challenge in the fervour of oral delivery, cannot always stand the colder criticism of the closet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Writers (especially those used to speaking publicly) should revise before submitting to print: effective spoken rhetoric may require pruning or reworking to survive close, dispassionate reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use observation of small events as political/poetic barometers
rubrics_metrics.description: You know I'm a feller thet keeps a skinned eye On the leetle events thet go skurryin' by, Coz it's of'ner by them than by gret ones you'll see Wut the p'litickle weather is likely to be.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attention to small, quotidian details yields reliable insight into larger moods (political or cultural). For writers, small observations can anchor larger themes or forecasts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid adopting played-out or foreignized sentimentalisms
rubrics_metrics.description: This makes 'em talk o' daisies, larks, an' things, Ez though we'd nothin' here that blows an' sings,-- (Why, I'd give more for one live bobolink Than a square mile o' larks in printer's ink,)--
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't lean on imported pastoral tropes when local flora/fauna and feeling will do better. Cultivate native imagery rather than defaulting to conventional pastoral stock.
